grammar.title: Grammar Focus: Integrated grammar and communication review

formula.label: Less accurate wording / prompt
formula.text: Improved wording — Reason

formula.label: I enjoy to walk.
formula.text: I enjoy walking. — Enjoy is followed by -ing.

formula.label: I would like joining the group.
formula.text: I would like to join the group. — Would like is followed by a to-infinitive.

formula.label: This hobby cures every illness.
formula.text: This is a leisure activity I enjoy. — State a preference without making an unsupported health claim.

practice: 1. Review should/must, present perfect, infinitives, gerunds, reported speech, conditionals and relative clauses.
2. Use enjoy + -ing and would like + to-infinitive to express preferences accurately.
3. A leisure preference is not a treatment prescription. Make measured statements and use only facts supplied in the assessment case.
Practice A. Complete or rewrite the sentences
1. Complete: A trainee should ___ for supervision when needed. (ask)

reading.title: Reading: Summative Assessment: Things I Like and Leisure Activities
body: The following student profiles are fictional. Dilnoza enjoys walking with a friend and has recently joined a reading group. She would like to protect one evening each week for leisure. Aziz prefers drawing, which he finds enjoyable after a busy day, but he does not enjoy competitive sport. Both students want a routine they can maintain; neither expects a hobby to solve every health problem. Physical activity can support health, but an appropriate choice depends on circumstances and preferences. [R8] For their college project, the students plan a short conversation about well-being. Dilnoza says, “If I finish my study tasks early, I will take a walk.” Aziz adds, “If I organised the group, I would include quieter activities.” The group meets in a room where students can discuss their preferences without pressure to reveal personal health information. The task is to explain a preference, listen to another person and agree a realistic activity, not to assess classmates’ mental health.
questions: 1. Which group has Dilnoza recently joined?
2. What does Aziz prefer doing?
3. Do either of the students expect a hobby to solve every health problem?
4. Which sentence describes an imagined situation?
5. What personal information are students not required to reveal?

listening.title: Listening
directions: Listen twice. First identify the situation; then complete each item with the missing detail. Use short answers. The full script is in the teacher section, not on this handout.
questions: 1. Dilnoza has recently joined a ___ group.
2. Aziz prefers ___.
3. The students will compare ___ options.
4. Neither option should pressure anyone to share personal ___ information.
5. The tutor asks for one communication skill to ___.
script: Read the complete script twice at a natural pace. Keep the wording stable between readings.

Tutor: What activity would you like to discuss for the project? Dilnoza: I enjoy walking with a friend, and I have recently joined a reading group. Aziz: I prefer drawing. If I organised the group, I would include a quiet activity as well. Tutor: What can you agree on? Dilnoza: If we finish our work early, we will compare two options. Aziz: Both options should be manageable, and neither should pressure anyone to share personal health information. Tutor: Good. Please choose the room where your group usually meets. Then explain the plan in your own words and identify one communication skill you want to improve.

speaking.outcome: Prepare with your own role card. Do not show it to your partner during the first exchange. Listen, ask for clarification and agree on a clear next step; then swap roles.
speaking.roleA: Student A: Student project coordinator
speaking.roleB: Student B: Group member
prompts: Prepare with your own role card. Do not show it to your partner during the first exchange. Listen, ask for clarification and agree on a clear next step; then swap roles.
Peer observation
Assessment reflection — after collection

After the scripts and written work have been collected, identify one successful clarification strategy and one grammar pattern to review. This is assessment reflection, not an additional culture topic.

practice a: 1. ask 2. tried 3. walking 4. The student said that she would ask a question. 5. where
reading 1–5: 1. A reading group. 2. Drawing. 3. No; neither does. 4. “If I organised the group, I would include quieter activities.” 5. Personal health information.
mini-quiz 1–6: 1. will start 2. would include 3. check 4. Neither 5. take 6. repeating
speaking: model response: “I enjoy drawing, which I find relaxing. I have recently tried a reading group. If our group agrees, we will choose an activity that feels manageable. I would like to protect one evening for leisure.”
culture / reflection: suggested response: Accept a specific reflection such as “I checked an unknown detail instead of guessing; I need to review past participles.”

Both activities seem manageable for me, although other students may prefer different options. I do not expect a hobby to solve every health problem; my goal is to protect time for something I value.
